analysis.investment_thesis: Alok Industries is a technically insolvent textile company with ₹26,106 Cr in borrowings against negative equity of ₹-21,527 Cr — the balance sheet is irreparably broken. Revenue has declined at -9% CAGR over nine years and the company has posted net losses for eight of the last ten years; there is no earnings power, no dividend, and no path to compounding visible.
key_strengths: 75% promoter holding post-NCLT resolution (Reliance Industries backstop provides some operational credibility)
Gross margin of 31.5% indicates the underlying product has pricing power if costs were manageable
OCF was positive in 4 of last 5 years, suggesting minimal operating cash generation exists
key_risks: Negative equity of ₹-21,527 Cr and borrowings of ₹26,106 Cr — debt-to-equity ratio is not even calculable; company is technically insolvent
Finance costs of ₹615 Cr consume 16.5% of ₹3,715 Cr revenue, making sustainable profitability nearly impossible without massive debt write-down
Revenue contraction at -9% CAGR over 9 years with no recovery trend — the business is structurally shrinking
red_flags: Negative book value (P/B of -0.33) — equity has been completely destroyed
EV/EBITDA of 320.8x is nonsensical — the market is pricing in a turnaround that the numbers do not support
Reserves are deeply negative at ₹-22,024 Cr in 2026, worsening every single year
NCLT insolvency resolution in 2019 wiped out original promoters — the 'other income' spikes of ₹7,063 Cr (2019) and ₹2,082 Cr (2020) were debt write-offs, not real earnings
Net losses every year from 2022–2026 despite post-resolution clean-up; operating margin remains negative at -4.51%
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Alok Industries failed catastrophically before its NCLT resolution in 2019, and the post-resolution entity has shown no meaningful recovery. Revenue has nearly halved from ₹8,723 Cr in 2017 to ₹3,715 Cr in 2026. The operating margin stands at -4.51%, ROCE at -3.25%, and net losses continue unabated — ₹744 Cr lost in FY2026 alone. The balance sheet is among the most distressed I have ever seen: ₹26,106 Cr in borrowings, near-zero cash of ₹25 Cr, and total equity of ₹-21,527 Cr. This company destroys value every single year with no sign of reversal.

From my investing discipline, I require a debt-to-equity below 0.3 and consistent profitability. Alok fails every single metric I care about — no profits, no dividends, no positive equity, no revenue growth, and no free cash flow consistency. The only reason this stock trades at all is speculative hope attached to the Reliance Industries stake. That is not investing; that is gambling. I would not touch this at any price — not at ₹14, not at ₹1. Capital preservation demands an immediate and unconditional pass.
